chapter: Detroit 1927: Pollack, Casa Loma, Atlantic City
title: The Pollack band visits the Greystone
summary: Pollack's musicians came to Detroit to hear the Greystone band; Challis recalls Teagarden and Glenn Miller.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: Well, we made that trip to Chicago and had a big kick -- got a big kick out of it and then we were hanging around the Greystone one night, about -- if the whole bunch of the Ben Pollack band didn't come in, they had come all the way from Chicago to listen to us, listen to the Greystone band. And that was well appreciated. But there they were, let's see, they had Jack Teagarden in the band then and I think Glenn Miller had given up the trombone and was just arranging.

Let's see, I don't know, McPartland -- there was another guy there too, beside McPartland, or after McPartland and he played very well. I forget what his name was. Jimmy told me one time what his name was, but I have forgotten.
But that's a band we really liked; they had a good beat.
